design_summary.scenario: Prepare a launch-ready domain shortlist for a developer workflow product from a business brief, public-brand examples, a candidate pool, and an archived RDAP availability snapshot.
why_skill_relevant: The core work matches the selected skill: understand the project, evaluate multiple naming options, check cross-TLD availability, and present ranked alternatives.
The required audit file forces the solver to examine every candidate/TLD pair instead of guessing a few names.
The shortlist, runner-up, and taken-domain outputs create clear verifier hooks around systematic availability checking and alternative selection.

main_tests: The audit covers every candidate and every allowed TLD, with correct availability states and deterministic scores.
The shortlist keeps one selected domain per base name and matches the top available base-wise options under the policy rules.
Runner-ups and rejected taken domains follow the same ordering logic as the main shortlist.
Outputs stay reproducible across reruns and remain consistent with the provided business brief and policy files.
guardrails: Input data remains unchanged while the bound skill stays available as runtime guidance.
Only the required output files are left in /root/output.
Selected domains must come from the provided availability snapshot rather than fabricated names.

control_condition_rule: with_skill and without_skill must differ only by environment/skills and corresponding runtime copy behavior
